history.notes:
REVISE: rubric items 1 and 2 fail. Every other item (3-13) holds. Nothing inside the 14 paths is wrong. The failures follow from the approved rule (Trellis branches hold only N, plan step 3). Under plan section 6 they are the author's decision, not a coding fault.

FAILED ITEMS
- Rubric 1 and 2: I re-ran the suite on the branch at dc513f7 and got 4 failed, 1150 passed, 38 skipped, 5 deselected, 1 xfailed (the KNOWN_ISSUES C3: INV-11 entry). All four tests are outside the list, pass at 1029fcc, and were not edited.
  (a) tests/regression/test_coarse_blasts_rows_by_signs.py:43. The precondition fails because the hole bridge's ends have ratios 0.65-1.05 and are now out of N.
  (b) tests/regression/test_evidence_diagnosis.py:114, build_k28(blasts=9). f^8(q0) has ratio 2.991 and is out of N, so T(q0) stops at f^7(q0) and the order-flip copy lies past the cut.
  (c) tests/helpers/laws.py:1520-1534 via test_open_p3_deep_runs[inversion_period2_10]. check_trellis_is_cut_at_the_pip_orbit iterates trellis.registry as the crossing set (I read it). It holds 38 (ratio 1.031), which is now out of N. This is an oracle written before N existed.
  (d) tests/regression/test_pip_orbit_cut.py:95 test_p2inv10_every_class_walks. 38 and 39 (ratios 1.03 and 2.33) were the base's reference pair. The reference moves to (30,31),(31,32) and the case drops to 6/6 classes.
  None of these is a fault the coder could fix inside the 14 paths. Plan section 6 stops the run here and takes it to the author. The question for the author: should a clause-1 point on the pip orbit shorten T(q0) (D10)? That one choice drives (b), k28 x8 (24/15/23 -> 4/4/4), and the k32 x9-10 change. Then for each test: (c) widen the oracle to N (one line in tests/helpers/laws.py); (a), (b), (d) rewrite the precondition or the build, or narrow the rule's reach. A re-plan has to add those files to the list.

CHECKED AND GOOD
- Correctness: I read the whole src diff. resolved_ids is the plan's two-clause rule. Clause 2 is judged as a pair by max(dev_a, dev_b), over the whole registry, grouped by (u_key, s_key) and consecutive in unstable cdist order, with node-identity adjacency on the original segments. The cache keys on _orders_version, which is correct: an iterate link does not move N. The seven readers each filter by N: BridgeIterator cut and sources :378, infer_iterates sources and candidates :109/:226, create_bridges :1803, _frozen_ids :1102, trim_stable_manifolds :2178, Trellis.from_workbench :422, StrongPip :169. The vote is gone. Detections are handed over sorted by (u, s) cdist, which keeps INT-7. No CLAUDE.md invariant is touched. Same-stability pairs are still never formed.
- Rubric 3: git diff --stat 1029fcc lists exactly the 14 paths (861+/276-).
- Rubric 4: the law-tier fingerprint guard passes in my run. The test engineer's byte-identical law dumps and the committed law-case pin (test_every_law_case_crossing_is_in_n, which passes on base and branch) show N equals the registry on all 11 law cases. Heteroclinic's minimum ratio is 3.038.
- Rubric 5: both greps are empty. Tangle.py goes from 1115 to 1052 lines (-63).
- Rubric 6: holds in substance. Each of the seven readers appears once. The extra hits are the definition's own docstrings, unresolved_crossings' internal call, and the Trellis.resolved_ids attribute that plan step 3 itself requires and StrongPip reads. Literally, 'nothing else' is contradicted by the plan's own step, so I do not grade this as a failure.
- Rubric 7, 8, 9, 10: committed tests cover them. The test engineer showed each fails on base where required.
- Rubric 11 and 12: the probe and rubric-12 script outputs in the evidence are consistent with the code I read.
- Rubric 13: the docstring has every required phrase.
- Break-it, re-run by me on an exported copy of dc513f7 (the control run is 30/30 green):
  (A) each detection compared to its own deviation instead of the pair max: the symmetric-pair and zig-zag tests fail.
  (B) a new check, not in the evidence: node-sharing adjacency in _polyline_gap turned off. 4 tests fail (symmetric pair, trellis branch, stable trim, one more), which closes the gap the evidence section 7 named.
  (C) StrongPip ignoring N: the strong-pip test fails.
- The test evidence is thorough and honest. Its k32 x9-10 finding (holes 58->56, closed 39->45, reliable False->True) is missing from the coder's report and belongs in the author's packet.

MINOR, does not move the grade
- Trellis.__init__ defaults resolved_ids to every registered id (Trellis.py:204). So the MinimalTrellis sparse snapshot, which shares the parent registry, reports unresolved detections as resolved. It is harmless today because no reader of N runs on it. Passing the parent's set would be safer.
- run_partner is not in the plan. It is used once, by the WARNING, and is acceptable.

PASS. All 13 rubric items hold. Items 1 and 3 are read as the author amended them on 2026-10-12 (the four files are added to the list, 18 paths). Branch refactor/resolved-crossings at 76d0710, base 1029fcc.

PREVIOUS FAILURES (rubric 1, 2): FIXED
- Full suite, run by me on 76d0710: 1157 passed, 38 skipped, 5 deselected, 1 xfailed. The only xfail is KNOWN_ISSUES C3/INV-11. Round 1 had 4 failures; all four now pass. The fifth failure the coder uncovered (test_open_p3_deep_runs[inversion_period2_10], where a law checked nothing) passes too. It was fixed in tests/cases.py (BUILDERS, now at 1e-6), which is on the list. test_open_p3_deep_runs.py itself was not edited.
- Rubric 2: the test engineer copied the reworked builds and tests into the 1029fcc base worktree and they pass there (8 passed). So the rewrites describe behaviour the old code also had.
- Rubric 3: git diff --name-only 1029fcc lists exactly the 18 paths. git diff dc513f7..HEAD -- src is empty, so items 4-13 stand as graded in round 1.

WERE THE TWO threshold=None TESTS WEAKENED? No.
The author's instruction was to rework preconditions or builds and never delete the defect a test guards. Both edits stay inside that.
- Every assertion line is unchanged (I read git diff dc513f7..HEAD).
- resolution_ratio_threshold = None is the documented public knob. It turns clause 1 off and leaves clause 2 on, and two new unit tests fail under a mutant that breaks either half.
- Both defects live downstream of N: the partition's sign rule (NUM-1/D6) and the evidence verdict (C21). That code runs the same whatever the threshold.
- My break-its, on a git-archive copy of HEAD (control run: 3/3 green):
  (i) StablePartition.py:1371 openings rule changed from == to !=: test_coarse_blasts_rows_by_signs fails, AssertionError ((42, 41), 41, 'outward', 'right'), on the targeted hole bridge.
  (ii) SymbolicDynamics.py:1221 changed to 'if False:' (an order flip is never diagnosed): test_an_order_flip_gives_no_verdict fails.
  (iii) laws.py:1526 N-skip removed: test_p2inv10_coarse_cut_holds_what_is_resolved fails, AssertionError (38, False, 3.17, 1.645), which is the round-1 failure.
  (iv) The opt-out removed from build_period3_coarse_blasts: the precondition 'the builder no longer makes an under-resolved hole bridge' fails. So the opt-out is load-bearing, and the precondition still guards against a vacuous pass.
- p2inv10, refined to 1e-6, is the author's suggested remedy. The new precondition (no unresolved detection) keeps it honest. The 1e-5 law build is kept by a new test, so the oracle's N clause is exercised: the test engineer's M1 showed it was otherwise unguarded.

FOR THE AUTHOR (these do not move the grade)
- tests/cases.py:594 and tests/regression/test_evidence_diagnosis.py:110 now guard NUM-1 and C21 only on detections the default N excludes. Under the default threshold no build anyone found reaches either defect. The coder offers a NOT_APPLICABLE mark or a unit-level re-guard instead. That is the author's choice; the present form is a legitimate build rework.
- test_pip_orbit_cut.py test_p2inv10_every_class_walks does not catch, by itself, a cut that drops only the stable half (M3). Four other tests in the same run catch it.
- Carried from round 1, still open: Trellis.py:204 defaults resolved_ids to the whole registry, which affects the MinimalTrellis sparse snapshot. The fix (pass parent.resolved_ids at MinimalTrellis.py:411) is outside the list. It is harmless today.

GOOD
- The round-2 edits are minimal: one skip condition in the oracle, one keyword with the law case's default unchanged (so the fingerprint guard is untouched), and docstrings that say why each build differs and cite Q13 (a) / B1.
- The test evidence is thorough and candid. Every mutant was restored and checked clean. The weak spots (M3, the reachability of tests a/b) are reported, not hidden.
